segments.text: Sloths are lazy. Well, that's not exactly true. They're just saving energy.
Sloths mostly eat leaves, and leaves give almost no energy. So their whole body runs in slow motion.
Here's the wild part. A single meal can take weeks to move through their stomach.
They climb down from their tree only about once a week. Just to poop.
In fact, they move so little that algae grows in their fur. It turns them a bit green, which helps them hide.
That's not all. Some sloths can turn their head about {270°|two hundred seventy degrees.}
And in water, sloths are surprisingly good swimmers. They move faster there than on land.
So sloths aren't lazy. They're just running on leaf power.
